title: $\mathcal O_{F,X}$ is finite free over $\mathcal O_{E,X}$
statement:
Let $E\subset F$ be finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside $\Qlb$, of degree $d=[F:E]$, and
let $X$ be a scheme. Then a choice of $\cO_E$-basis $b_1,\dots,b_d$ of $\cO_F$ induces
isomorphisms of $\cO_{E,X}$-modules, resp. $E_X$-modules,
$$
\cO_{E,X}^{\,d}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\cO_{F,X},\qquad E_X^{\,d}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }F_X,
\qquad (a_i)\mapsto\textstyle\sum_ia_ib_i ,
$$
compatible with the maps $\cO_{E,X}\to E_X$ and $\cO_{F,X}\to F_X$ and with inverse image
along morphisms of schemes. In particular $\cO_{F,X}$ and $F_X$ are flat
([lem-sfb-subfield-flat]).

proof.text: Use the adopted source theorem PadicAlgCl.finite_integersMap for the actual integer inclusion. The lower integer ring is a PID, both integer rings are integrally closed in their fraction fields, and finiteness makes the upper ring integral over the lower one. Thus IsIntegralClosure.of_isIntegrallyClosed identifies the upper integer ring as the integral closure. Mathlib IsIntegralClosure.module_free and IsIntegralClosure.rank give a basis indexed by Fin [F:E]. This is the private integral_basis_exists proof, with all scalar towers explicitly supplied.

For any chosen integral basis, its finite-sum map from the product of integer rings is continuous and bijective. Its domain is compact and its target Hausdorff, so its inverse coordinate maps are continuous. The proved private continuous_basis_iso applies the existing continuousAddHom and continuousLinearAction API from CondensedSubfieldBasis to the coordinates and basis vectors. Form the biproduct lift and desc, and check their inverse identities sectionwise using sum_repr and coordinate evaluation on basis vectors. Its injection equation is exactly finiteCoefficientPointSummand.

The point inverse image is a strong monoidal left adjoint, hence preserves coproducts and is additive. Apply monoidalFiniteFreeTransport. Compose its result with mapModComapIso and the identity underlying isomorphism from the transported regular module to the regular module of the transported ring. This gives the integral isomorphism and its exact summand formulas on every scheme.

Localize the chosen integral basis using Mathlib Basis.localizationLocalization and IsIntegralClosure.isLocalization. Its image is a field basis consisting of exactly the same vectors. The field coordinates are continuous after restriction of scalars to Q_ell. Apply continuous_basis_iso and the same monoidal pullback construction to obtain the rational isomorphism with the prescribed rational summands. This performs the rational basis passage directly on the actual coefficient fields; no sequential sheaf-localization comparison is necessary.

The integral-to-field summand square is equality of the two pointwise formulas phi(a)*b in the upper field. Apply the point inverse-image functor and its composition equation. For either coefficient ring, rewrite the injection composite using the established summand formula; naturality of upperStarFromPointComp on that point summand is exactly the requested inverse-image square.

Use the proved generic finiteCoordinateIso construction and its naturality from FiniteFreeScalarCoordinates to identify scalar extension followed by restriction with the finite-power functor. Finite powers preserve limits. The module forgetful functors create limits, so composing with the lower forgetful functor and reflecting through the upper forgetful functor proves integral finite-limit preservation. The rational clause is the existing source instance preservesFiniteLimits_extendScalars_padicSubfieldRingObjMap.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $E\subset F$ be finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside $\Qlb$, of degree $d=[F:E]$, and
let $X$ be a scheme. Then a choice of $\cO_E$-basis $b_1,\dots,b_d$ of $\cO_F$ induces
isomorphisms of $\cO_{E,X}$-modules, resp. $E_X$-modules,
$$
\cO_{E,X}^{\,d}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\cO_{F,X},\qquad E_X^{\,d}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }F_X,
\qquad (a_i)\mapsto\textstyle\sum_ia_ib_i ,
$$
compatible with the maps $\cO_{E,X}\to E_X$ and $\cO_{F,X}\to F_X$ and with inverse image
along morphisms of schemes. In particular $\cO_{F,X}$ and $F_X$ are flat
([lem-sfb-subfield-flat]).

proof.text:
$\cO_F$ is a finite torsion-free, hence free, module over the discrete valuation ring
$\cO_E$, of rank $d$. The map $\cO_E^d\to\cO_F$, $(a_i)\mapsto\sum a_ib_i$, is a continuous
$\cO_E$-linear bijection between compact Hausdorff spaces, hence a homeomorphism. So for
every profinite $S$ it induces a bijection $C(S,\cO_E)^d=C(S,\cO_E^d)\to C(S,\cO_F)$, natural in
$S$ and $C(S,\cO_E)$-linear: an isomorphism of condensed $\underline{\cO_E}$-modules
$\underline{\cO_E}^{\,d}\cong\underline{\cO_F}$ ([det-def-sfb-condensed-ring]). Apply the
additive, monoidal functor $p_X^*$ ([det-def-sfb-pullback-from-point]): it gives
$\cO_{E,X}^{\,d}\cong\cO_{F,X}$ as $\cO_{E,X}$-modules. Inverting $\ell$
([det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-invert-ell]) gives $E_X^{\,d}\cong F_X$, and the two
isomorphisms are compatible with $\cO\to E$ by construction. Compatibility with inverse
image follows from naturality of $f^{-1}p_Y^*\cong p_X^*$.
